note: Reference skeleton of the official AP Statistics CED framework: unit/topic numbers and skill codes are official identifiers; objective statements are short paraphrases (no verbatim CED prose). Skill sub-codes are indicative and should be verified against the official CED during QA.

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: What Can We Learn from Data?

objectives.statement: Explain how statistics can be used to answer questions about data and variation.

topics.title: The Language of Variation: Variables

objectives.statement: Distinguish categorical from quantitative variables and describe the role of variation in data.

topics.title: Representing a Categorical Variable with Tables

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret frequency and relative frequency tables for a categorical variable.

topics.title: Representing a Categorical Variable with Graphs

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret bar charts and pie charts for categorical data.

topics.title: Representing a Quantitative Variable with Graphs

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret dotplots, stemplots, and histograms to display the distribution of a quantitative variable.
Read and compare graphical displays of quantitative data, including identifying unusual features.

topics.title: Describing the Distribution of a Quantitative Variable

objectives.statement: Describe the shape, center, and spread of a distribution of a quantitative variable in context.

topics.title: Summary Statistics for a Quantitative Variable

objectives.statement: Calculate and interpret measures of center (mean, median) and measures of spread (range, IQR, standard deviation).
Explain how outliers and skew affect summary statistics such as mean, median, range, IQR, and standard deviation.

topics.title: Graphical Representations of Summary Statistics

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret boxplots and the five-number summary for a quantitative variable.

topics.title: Comparing Distributions of a Quantitative Variable

objectives.statement: Compare distributions of a quantitative variable across groups using center, spread, shape, and outliers.

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: Are Variables Related?

objectives.statement: Explain how statistics can be used to investigate relationships between two variables.

topics.title: Representing Two Categorical Variables

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables for two categorical variables.

topics.title: Statistics for Two Categorical Variables

objectives.statement: Compute and interpret row, column, and overall relative frequencies in a two-way table.

topics.title: Representing the Relationship Between Two Quantitative Variables

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret scatterplots to display the relationship between two quantitative variables.

topics.title: Correlation

objectives.statement: Describe the strength and direction of a linear relationship and explain properties of the correlation coefficient.

topics.title: Linear Regression Models

objectives.statement: Interpret the slope and intercept of a least-squares regression line and use it to make predictions.

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: Do the Data We Collected Tell the Truth?

objectives.statement: Explain why sampling and study design matter for the validity of conclusions.

topics.title: Introduction to Planning a Study

objectives.statement: Identify the population, sample, and parameters or statistics of interest in a study.

topics.title: Random Sampling and Data Collection

objectives.statement: Describe and use simple random sampling and other probability sampling methods.

topics.title: Potential Problems with Sampling

objectives.statement: Explain sampling bias, nonresponse, undercoverage, and response bias and their effects.

topics.title: Introduction to Experimental Design

objectives.statement: Distinguish observational studies from experiments and explain the role of random assignment.

topics.title: Selecting an Experimental Design

objectives.statement: Describe completely randomized, blocked, and matched-pairs experimental designs.

topics.title: Inference and Experiments

objectives.statement: Explain how random assignment supports cause-and-effect conclusions and how random sampling supports generalizing.

units.title: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: Random and Non-Random Patterns?

objectives.statement: Explain how probability models randomness and variation.

topics.title: Estimating Probabilities Using Simulation

objectives.statement: Use simulations to estimate probabilities of outcomes from a process or chance model.

topics.title: Introduction to Probability

objectives.statement: Apply the basic rules of probability to compute probabilities of outcomes.

topics.title: Mutually Exclusive Events

objectives.statement: Determine when events are mutually exclusive and find probabilities of their union.

topics.title: Conditional Probability

objectives.statement: Compute and interpret conditional probabilities and use them in two-way tables.

topics.title: Independent Events and Unions of Events

objectives.statement: Determine independence of events and use the multiplication rule for independent events.

topics.title: Introduction to Random Variables and Probability Distributions

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret discrete probability distributions for random variables.

topics.title: Mean and Standard Deviation of Random Variables

objectives.statement: Calculate the mean and standard deviation of a discrete random variable.

topics.title: Combining Random Variables

objectives.statement: Find the mean and variance of sums and differences of independent random variables.

topics.title: Introduction to the Binomial Distribution

objectives.statement: Determine whether a situation fits a binomial setting and calculate binomial probabilities.

topics.title: Parameters for a Binomial Distribution

objectives.statement: Find the mean and standard deviation of a binomial random variable and use them in context.

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: Why Is My Sample Not Like Yours?

objectives.statement: Explain what a sampling distribution is and why statistics vary from sample to sample.

topics.title: The Normal Distribution, Revisited

objectives.statement: Use the Normal distribution to describe distributions and find percentiles and proportions.

topics.title: The Central Limit Theorem

objectives.statement: Describe the sampling distribution of a sample mean and sample proportion using the Central Limit Theorem.

topics.title: Biased and Unbiased Point Estimates

objectives.statement: Define and compare biased versus unbiased point estimates and standard error.

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: Why Be Normal?

objectives.statement: Explain how the sampling distribution of a sample proportion enables inference about a population proportion.

topics.title: Constructing a Confidence Interval for a Population Proportion

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret a confidence interval for a population proportion and state its conditions.

topics.title: Justifying a Claim Based on a Confidence Interval

objectives.statement: Decide whether a claimed value of a population proportion is plausible given a confidence interval.

topics.title: Setting Up a Test for a Population Proportion

objectives.statement: State hypotheses and conditions for a one-sample proportion z-test.

topics.title: Interpreting P-Values

objectives.statement: Interpret a p-value in context as a probability under the null hypothesis.

topics.title: Concluding a Test for a Population Proportion

objectives.statement: Make a conclusion for a one-sample proportion z-test in context and compare it with a significance level.

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: Should I Worry About Error Intervals?

objectives.statement: Explain how the sampling distribution of a sample mean enables inference about a population mean.

topics.title: Constructing a Confidence Interval for a Population Mean

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret a confidence interval for a population mean using a t-interval and state its conditions.

topics.title: Justifying a Claim about a Population Mean Based on a Confidence Interval

objectives.statement: Decide whether a claimed value of a population mean is plausible given a confidence interval.

topics.title: Setting Up a Test for a Population Mean

objectives.statement: State hypotheses and conditions for a one-sample t-test for a population mean.

topics.title: Interpreting P-Values for a Test of a Population Mean

objectives.statement: Interpret a p-value for a one-sample t-test in context.

topics.title: Concluding a Test for a Population Mean

objectives.statement: Make a conclusion for a one-sample t-test in context and compare it with a significance level.

topics.title: Justifying a Claim about the Difference of Two Means Based on a Confidence Interval

objectives.statement: Construct, interpret, and reason with a confidence interval for the difference of two population means.

topics.title: Setting Up a Test for the Difference of Two Population Means

objectives.statement: State hypotheses and conditions for a two-sample t-test for the difference of two population means.

topics.title: Interpreting P-Values for Tests of the Difference of Two Means

objectives.statement: Interpret a p-value for a two-sample t-test in context.

topics.title: Concluding a Test for the Difference of Two Means

objectives.statement: Make a conclusion for a two-sample t-test in context and compare it with a significance level.

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: Are My Results Unexpected?

objectives.statement: Explain why chi-square tests are used to compare observed counts with expected counts.

topics.title: The Chi-Square Statistic

objectives.statement: Calculate the chi-square statistic from observed and expected counts.

topics.title: The Chi-Square Test for Goodness of Fit

objectives.statement: Run a chi-square goodness-of-fit test and interpret its results in context.

topics.title: The Chi-Square Test for Homogeneity

objectives.statement: Run a chi-square test for homogeneity and interpret its results in context.

topics.title: The Chi-Square Test for Independence

objectives.statement: Run a chi-square test for independence and interpret its results in context.

topics.title: Selecting an Appropriate Inference Procedure

objectives.statement: Select the appropriate chi-square test (goodness of fit, homogeneity, independence) for a given context.

topics.title: Introducing Statistics: Do Those Points Align?

objectives.statement: Explain how inference about the slope of a regression model lets us reason about a bivariate population.

topics.title: Confidence Intervals for the Slope of a Regression Model

objectives.statement: Construct and interpret a confidence interval for the slope of a least-squares regression line.

topics.title: Justifying a Claim about the Slope of a Regression Model Based on a Confidence Interval

objectives.statement: Decide whether a claimed slope value is plausible given a confidence interval and interpret association versus causation.

topics.title: Setting Up a Test for the Slope of a Regression Model

objectives.statement: State hypotheses and conditions for a t-test for the slope of a regression line.

topics.title: Interpreting P-Values for Tests of the Slope of a Regression Model

objectives.statement: Interpret a p-value for a slope test in context.

topics.title: Concluding a Test for the Slope of a Regression Model

objectives.statement: Make a conclusion for a slope test in context and compare it with a significance level.
